correctness.rationale: The nonzero rank-one substitution R(x)=f(x)u reduces the identity to u^2=lambda*u and functional eigenrelations for left/right multiplication by u; lambda=0 forces both to annihilate uA+Au, and lambda!=0 yields a unique normalized idempotent e with functional in the two disjoint Peirce-corner dual spaces. The triangular nilpotent radical conjugates each idempotent with k diagonal 1s to its diagonal word, with exactly q^{k(n-k)} lifts, while the Peirce dimensions are binary inversion counts; Gaussian inversion enumerators yield B_n(q)=2 sum_{k=1}^{n-1} q^{k(n-k)}([n k]_q-binomial(n,k)). For T_3 the square-zero lines are q+q+1 with annihilator codimensions 2,2,1 and count A_3=3q^5-2q-1; adding B_3 gives total 3q^5+4q^4+4q^3-8q^2-2q-1. All q prime powers, n>=1, rank-one operators only. Fresh independently composed F2 direct six-dimensional basis-identity test gave exactly 155 operators (91 nilpotent-image, 64 idempotent-image); symbolic inversion sum checked several n. These finite tests are corroboration, not a universal proof.
